title: Foreground/Background Cache Thaw Investigation — personal scratchpad
content:
Goal:
Quickly understand how background tenant noise + periodic low QPS windows cause cache thawing (KV cache miss storm) for foreground low-latency requests. Build minimal reproducible workload and capture empirical latency/kv-hit profiles, hypothesize mitigations.

Motivation/context:
- Product: low-latency chat endpoint serving many multi-tenant apps. Some customers get repeated short bursts with long idle tails (few minutes).
- Observed: after a ~2–10m idle, a foreground request sees P99 spike ~3–5x for first few tokens; KV cache hit rate drops sharply. Suspect eviction + cold-start of attention key/value caches on GPU memory + kernel trampolining for quantized models.

Hypothesis:
1) Background batch jobs (low-priority tenants) temporarily evict KV cache or cause GPU memory pressure -> foreground requests get no warm cache.
2) Even without eviction, the runtime defers kernel specialization for long-tail sequence lengths, leading to first-request kernel selection jitter.
3) Small prefix (1–3 tokens) of foreground requests is dominated by setup/transfer overhead; once warmed, steady-state is fine.

Testbed:
- Model: rl-13b-4q (approx. 13B q4_k_mixed) loaded on single A100-80GB instance (dedicated pool)
- Runtime: serving-runtime@main (with latest batching and kv cache write-through patch)
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency (first token and full completion), tokens/sec, kv-cache-hit-rate, GPU util, memory usage, kernel-switch counts (instrumented), request traces (trace id -> timestamps)
- Tools: wrk2 for arrival shaping (modified to do chat-like short prompts), small python harness to inject background batches, Prometheus scrape at 5s, perf tracing.

Workload scenarios (all runs 20m each unless noted):
- Baseline (Run 0): steady QPS=10, single-tenant foreground only (short prompts length=40 tokens).
- Run A: cold idle window 6m, then a single foreground spike QPS=25 for 30s. No background jobs during idle.
- Run B: background churn: continuous background low-priority batch jobs qps=5 (long sequences 512 tokens) running through entire idle window -> evictions expected, then foreground spike same as Run A.
- Run C: same as B but background churn stopped 30s before foreground spike (to test thaw delay).
- Run D: adaptive-priority enabled (foreground preemption) with background at qps=5; identical to B.

Raw results (aggregated):
- Run 0 (baseline): p50-first=22ms, p95-first=36ms, p99-first=58ms; kv-hit=98.1%; tokens/sec=750.
- Run A (cold idle, no bg): p50-first=120ms, p95-first=300ms, p99-first=520ms; kv-hit=12.5% (first 10s), then recovered to 94% after ~15s; tokens/sec (first 10s)=210 -> steady 730.
- Run B (background churn through idle): p50-first=180ms, p95-first=420ms, p99-first=980ms; kv-hit=4.2% first 30s; kernel-switch-events spike (avg 6 switches per request vs 1 baseline); GPU mem transient high ~78–95% during churn; sustained >90% eviction markers in runtime logs.
- Run C (bg stopped 30s prior): p50-first=98ms, p95-first=210ms, p99-first=420ms; kv-hit=35% first 20s then to 88% by 25s.
- Run D (adaptive-priority): p50-first=36ms, p95-first=62ms, p99-first=120ms; kv-hit=86% immediately; kernel-switches ~1.6 per request.

Observations / notes:
- Cold idle alone (Run A) causes a large setup penalty: large portion of p99 is in data transfer + kv cache miss population. The miss storm self-heals as requests populate the KV cache and compiled kernels are JIT-ed/selected.
- Background churn (Run B) makes everything worse: evictions observed and regeneration competes with slow background longer sequences that keep memory occupied.
- Stopping background work shortly before foreground (Run C) helps but requires ~20–30s slack to recover cache warmth.
- Prioritizing foreground and allowing preemption (Run D) massively reduces customer-visible tail. This matches the hypothesis that eviction + kernel selection jitter are both contributors and that foreground isolation reduces both impacts.
- Kernel-switch metric correlates well with P99: more switches -> higher P99. Likely because runtime falls back to slower kernels when mixed precision/sequence characteristics change.

Micro-trace (example ids trimmed):
- trace 20260228-001: arrival=0.0s, queue wait=2ms, load-kv-miss-major=120ms, transfer=6ms, first-token=154ms.
- trace 20260228-023: arrival=12.2s, queue wait=1ms, cache-populate=18ms, kernel-specialize=24ms, first-token=48ms.

Quick ASCII heatmap (kv-hit % by second after spike start) — Run B:
[0s] 4% | [5s] 7% | [10s] 12% | [20s] 26% | [30s] 42% | [60s] 78%

Preliminary conclusions:
- Operational mitigation with highest bang-for-buck: implement foreground preemption / reservation (short-lived soft reservations) so that a small portion of KV cache + some GPU memory can be reserved for latency-critical tenants. This prevents background batch jobs from evicting the tiny warm cache that foreground needs. (Matches Run D improvements.)
- Second: implement a lightweight cold-warm probe: when a tenant has been idle >60s, perform a tiny warmup probe (1–2 token infer) at low-priority before first real request to populate KV cache and trigger kernel paths. Need to weigh cost vs latency benefit.
- Third: reduce kernel-trampolining by keeping a small cache of compiled kernels for common sequence-length buckets (1–8, 9–64, 65–256). Avoid JIT on first request for these buckets.

Risks / tradeoffs:
- Reserving GPU memory reduces overall batch throughput (cost). Need to quantify: reserve 1–2 GB per GPU per node vs expected revenue/latency SLO impact.
- Warmup probes add extra small-cost requests; must rate-limit and backoff (don't do probes when traffic already high).

Next steps / experiments:
1) Run cost/throughput analysis: simulate reserve 1GB memory for foreground tenants across cluster mix and measure throughput delta. (Create spreadsheet).
2) Implement probe PoC in harness; measure cost (ppp) and user-visible p99 reduction for a set of long-tail tenants.
3) Add kernel-cache experiment: maintain compiled-kernel cache for small seq buckets, benchmark first-request improvements.
4) Add a run mixing many tenants (50) with 3% foreground critical, measure scatter impact.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Upload logs + flamegraphs to PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2486 (I already added initial tracer).
- Slack thread with Priya: ask infra for realistic cluster mix samples (how many long-serving background batch tenants do we have?).
- Linear: link INF-8123: propose "foreground reservation" epi.

Attachments (local):
- prom-scrapes-20260228.zip (contains time series used to compute heatmaps)
- perf-traces-20260228/ (subset with kernel-switch logs)

End of scratchpad.

(Feel free to reuse any of this in a short postmortem; copy/paste friendly. Will redact trace ids before uploading public notes.)
